title: Aptamer-facilitated Protein Isolation from Cells
protocol: Centrifuge positive and negative cell lysates at 17,500 × g for 1 hour at 4 °C.
Discard the pellets.
Divide supernatants into 10 µL aliquots and store at -80 °C.
Perform SDS-PAGE with the positive cell lysate to ensure the target protein is in the soluble fraction.
Measure total protein concentration in both positive and negative cell lysates using a BCA protein assay kit, following manufacturer’s instructions.
Rinse every new capillary with four capillary volumes of 100 mM HCl.
Rinse every new capillary with four capillary volumes of 100 mM NaOH.
Rinse every new capillary with four capillary volumes of ddH2O.
Rinse every new capillary with four capillary volumes of RB.
Repeat rinsing immediately before and after every CE run.
Prepare 10 µL of a 500 µM naive DNA library in SB.
Heat the mixture to 94 °C.
Cool down the mixture to 20 °C at a rate of 0.5 °C per second.
Treat all future DNA library and aptamer samples in this manner.
Prepare a 100 µM solution of the temperature-treated DNA library in 100 µL SB.
Prepare a 10 μL sample of equilibrium mixture with 10 μM DNA library and 100 μM of each masking DNAs.
Incubate the mixture for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Inject 150 nL of the mixture into the capillary.
Perform NECEEM in RB at 375 V cm⁻¹ with normal polarity and positive electrode at the injection end.
Determine the migration time of the DNA library to the end of the capillary.
Prepare a new equilibrium mixture with 10 μM DNA library, 20 μg mL⁻¹ of positive cell lysate, and 100 nM of fluorescein.
Incubate this mixture for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Inject 150 nL of the new mixture into the capillary.
Perform NECEEM in RB at 375 V cm⁻¹ with normal polarity and positive electrode at the injection end.
Determine the migration time of fluorescein to the end of the capillary.
Determine the relative elution time of fluorescein compared to the free DNA.
Run the sample in CE as described in step 9.
Observe peaks corresponding to species other than fluorescein and free DNA.
Prepare three 10 µL equilibrium mixtures with varying concentrations of masking DNAs.
Mix 10 µM of DNA library, 20 µg/mL positive cell lysate, 100 nM of fluorescein, and 100 µM masking DNA in the first mixture.
Mix 10 µM of DNA library, 20 µg/mL positive cell lysate, 100 nM of fluorescein, and 1 mM masking DNA in the second mixture.
Mix 10 µM of DNA library, 20 µg/mL positive cell lysate, 100 nM of fluorescein, and 10 mM masking DNA in the third mixture.
Incubate each equilibrium mixture for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Perform NECEEM analysis as described in step 9 on the incubated mixtures.
Observe the effect of varying masking DNA concentrations on lysate peaks.
Select the lowest masking DNA concentration that significantly suppresses the peaks without exceeding 10 mM.
Rinse the capillary with 4 capillary volumes of RNase-AWAY solution before rinsing as described in step 5.
Prepare a 10 µL equilibrium mixture for positive selection.
Mix 10 µM of DNA library, 20 µg/mL positive cell lysate, 100 nM of fluorescein, and the determined concentration of masking DNAs from step 15.
Incubate the equilibrium mixture for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Initiate NECEEM as described.
Place a tube with 5 μL of SB at the capillary outlet.
Collect the eluent from the beginning of CE run until the elution of the fluorescein peak.
Briefly pause the electric current when the fluorescein peak is eluting.
Switch the outlet of the capillary into an outlet containing RB.
Continue the electric current after switching outlets.
Stop the separation after the free DNA component of the equilibrium mixture elutes.
Incubate the collected fraction for 15 min at room temperature.
Rinse the capillary with 4 capillary volumes of RNase-AWAY solution before rinsing as described in step 5.
Prepare 10 μL equilibrium mixture containing 5 μL of the DNA fraction from step 19, 20 μg mL-1 of negative cell lysate, and 100 nM of fluorescein.
Add the determined concentration of masking DNAs to the equilibrium mixture from step 15.
Incubate the equilibrium mixture for 10 min at room temperature.
Perform NECEEM as described in step 9 with modifications.
Place a reservoir containing RB at the capillary outlet before starting NECEEM.
Briefly pause the electric current when the peak corresponding to fluorescein starts eluting during NECEEM.
Switch the outlet of the capillary into a tube with 5 μL of SB when pausing the current.
Continue collecting eluents for 5 minutes after the expected elution time of the free DNA component.

Set up 20 µL amplification reaction mixture for the fraction collected in step 22, including components as described: 10 µL of real-time PCR master mix with SYBR Green, 0.6 µL forward primer (to 300 nM), 0.6 µL reverse primer (to 300 nM), 1 µL template, and 7.8 µL ddH2O.
Amplify the reactions using a PCR program with a denaturation step of 180 s at 94 °C for cycle 1.
For cycles 2-40, perform a denaturation step of 10 s at 94 °C, an annealing step of 10 s at 56 °C, and a polymerization step of 10 s at 72 °C.
Hold the reaction at 4 °C.
Determine the number of cycles required for the reaction mixture to generate the product at a level of 50–60% of the maximum.
Set up a 40 µL amplification reaction mixture with the components as described in Table 3.
Add 10x PCR buffer to the reaction mixture (4 µL).
Pipette FAM-Forward primer into the reaction mixture (1.2 µL).
Pipette Biotin-Reverse primer into the reaction mixture (1.2 µL).
Add dNTPs to the reaction mixture (0.8 µL).
Add Taq DNA polymerase to the reaction mixture (0.4 µL).
Transfer 2 µL of template into the reaction mixture.
Add ddH2O to the reaction mixture (30.4 µL).
Set up a 40 µL control mixture with components as described in Table 3, but using ddH2O instead of the template.
Amplify the samples from steps 26 and 27 using the PCR program detailed in Table 4.
Perform the number of cycles that was determined to be optimal for amplification of the pool.
Denature the template DNA at 94 °C for 30 seconds.
For cycles 2 to optimum: Denature the DNA at 94 °C for 10 seconds, anneal at 55 °C for 10 seconds, and extend at 72 °C for 10 seconds.
Hold reaction mixture at 4 °C.
Transfer 5 µL of each amplification product into new sample tubes.
Precondition a 50-cm capillary as specified in the protocol.
Perform NECEEM on each sample using the preconditioned 50-cm capillary.
Set up an asymmetric PCR amplification reaction mixture for products from previous steps.
Add 4 µL of 10x PCR buffer to the reaction mixture.
Pipette 4 µL of FAM-Forward primer (10 µM) diluted to a final concentration of 1 µM into the reaction mixture.
Add 0.2 µL of Biotin-Reverse primer (10 µM) diluted to a final concentration of 50 nM to the reaction mixture.
Pipette 0.8 µL of dNTPs (10 mM) diluted to a final concentration of 200 nM into the mixture.
Add 0.4 µL of _Taq_ DNA polymerase (5 units/mL) diluted to a final concentration of 0.05 units/mL to the reaction mixture.
Transfer 2 µL of template DNA to the reaction mixture.
Add 28.6 µL of ddH2O to complete the 40 µL amplification reaction volume.
Amplify the reactions using the PCR program detailed in table 4.
Perform 15 amplification cycles without measuring the fluorescence signal.
Aliquot 20 µL streptavidin magnetic beads into an empty microcentrifuge tube.
Wash the beads twice with 200 µL BWB, removing excess solution after each wash.
Mix 40 µL of PCR-amplified samples from step 28 with 40 µL BWB.
Resuspend the washed beads in the sample solution and gently mix.
Incubate at room temperature for 20 min, gently mixing every five minutes.
Pull down the beads using a magnetic separator and collect the supernatant.
Load the supernatant onto molecular cut-off filters.
Discard the beads after loading the supernatant.
Centrifuge the molecular cut-off filters with the supernatant at 7,000 × g for 20 minutes at 15° C.
Load 200 µL of SB on to the filter and repeat centrifugation step.
Wash the filters in this manner three more times, discarding flow-through as the test tube fills.
Load 15 µL of SB on to the filter and incubate without centrifugation for 30 min at 15° C.
Place the filter upside-down into a new clean test tube.
Centrifuge the filter at 7,000 × g for 10 minutes at 15° C.
Collect the eluted fraction and discard the filters.
Store amplified aptamer pools at –20 °C for several years.
Prepare dilutions of the FAM-Forward primer: 50nM, 200 nM, 500nM, and 1 µM.
Perform NECEEM with each dilution of the FAM-labeled primer to obtain a standard curve.
Plot the heights of the produced peaks against primer concentrations.
Use temperature treatment on 5 μL of aptamer pool from step 40 as described in step 6.
Prepare an equilibrium mixture with: 1 µL of aptamer pool, 20 µg mL-1 of positive cell lysate, 100 nM of fluorescein, and the concentration of masking DNAs used in step 15.
Incubate the equilibrium mixture for 10 min at room temperature.
Use a 50-cm capillary for the CE run.
Rinse the capillary as described in step 5.
Inject 50 nL of the equilibrium mixture from step 44 into the capillary.
Run NECEEM in RB at 375 V cm⁻¹ with normal polarity and positive electrode at the injection end.
Compare the resultant electropherogram to the one produced in step 12.
Suspect peaks that increase in area correspond to complexes between the target protein and the DNA aptamers.
Calculate the bulk EC₅₀ value of the aptamer pool using equation 1 with the combined areas of suspected peaks.
In equation 1, Ttot and DNAtot are the total concentrations of the target and DNA, respectively.
A₁ is the area of the peak of free DNA divided by the migration time of free DNA.
A₂ is the area of the peak of DNA that dissociated from the complex during NECEEM divided by the migration time of free DNA.
A₃ is the area of the peak of the intact complex that reached the detector divided by the migration time of the complex.
Set up a 120 µL amplification reaction mixture.
Add 12 µL of 10x PCR buffer.
Pipette 3.6 µL of biotin-Forward primer (to 300 nM).
Pipette 3.6 µL of reverse primer (to 300 nM).
Add 2.4 µL of dNTPs (to 200 nM).
Add 1.2 µL of Taq DNA polymerase (to 0.05 units/mL).
Add 6 µL of template.
Pipette 91.2 µL of ddH2O.
Amplify the reactions using the PCR program described in table 4 for 15 cycles.
Set up 120 µL PCR amplification reactions.
Add 12 µL of 10x PCR buffer.
Pipette 12 µL of biotin-Forward primer (to 1 µM).
Pipette 0.6 µL of reverse primer (to 50 nM).
Add 2.4 µL of dNTPs (to 200 nM).
Add 1.2 µL of Taq DNA polymerase (to 0.05 units/mL).
Add 6 µL of product from amplification in step 52.
Pipette 91.2 µL of ddH2O.
Amplify the reactions using the PCR program described in table 4 for 15 cycles.
Load the product of the PCR amplification onto molecular cut-off filters.
Centrifuge the molecular cut-off filters with the supernatant from step 55 at 7,000 × g for 20 minutes at 15°C.
Load 200 µL of SB onto the filter and repeat centrifugation at 7,000 × g for 20 minutes at 15°C.
Wash the filters in this manner three more times, discarding the flow-through as the test tube becomes filled.
Load 15 µL of SB onto the filter and incubate without centrifugation for 30 min at 15°C.
Place the filter upside-down into a new clean test tube and centrifuge at 7,000 × g for 10 minutes at 15°C.
Collect the eluted fraction and discard the filters. The collected fraction contains the biotinylated DNA aptamer pool.
Use temperature treatment on 15 µL of biotinylated aptamer pool from step 60, as described in step 6.
Treat a sample of 500 µM naive DNA library as described in step 6 and prepare 100 µL of 100 µM naive DNA library in SB.
Prepare 50 µL equilibrium mixtures with each of the samples from steps 60 and 61: 15 µL of DNA sample, 20 µg/mL of positive cell lysate, and the concentration of masking DNAs as in step 48.
Incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Aliquot 50 µL streptavidin beads into an empty test tube.
Wash the beads twice with 200 µL bead washing buffer.
Precipitate the beads from the solution with a magnetic bead separator after each wash.
Add the pull-down samples to the beads after the final washing step.
Incubate at room temperature for 20 min, gently mixing every five minutes.
Pull down the beads from the solution using a magnetic separator and separate the beads and supernatant.
Preserve the supernatant for further analysis through SDS-PAGE.
Wash the beads three times with 100 µL of bead washing buffer.
Precipitate the beads from the solution with a magnetic bead separator after each wash.
Remove the BWB and add SDS-containing loading buffer according to the employed SDS-PAGE protocol.
Incubate at 99 °C for 5 min.
Pull down the beads from the solution using a magnetic separator and collect the supernatant.
Load directly onto a polyacrylamide gel for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Perform SDS-PAGE analysis on the pull-downs by the DNA aptamer pool.
Perform SDS-PAGE analysis on the naive DNA library pull-downs.
Perform SDS-PAGE analysis on the supernatant samples from step 66.
Stain the gel with Coomassie Blue dye.
Analyze the results of SDS-PAGE to determine aptamers’ ability to selectively isolate the target protein.
Determine the level of cross-reactivity of the aptamer pool with non-target components of the cell lysate.
